newsitem.title: USA: FBI arrests fourth suspect in Spokane bombings.
newsitem.headline: FBI arrests fourth suspect in Spokane bombings.

text.p: With the prosecution about to rest in the trial of three white supremacists accused of two 1996 bombings and bank robberies, FBI agents Thursday arrested a fourth suspect they had long been seeking.
Brian Ratigan, 38, of Sandpoint, Idaho, was arrested as he was about to board a train for Albany, New York, with his wife and two children, FBI officials said at a news conference.
He did not resist and was charged with conspiracy and bank robbery stemming from the attacks in April and July, which prosecutors say were motivated by the right-wing religious beliefs of the men.

In the first attack, a newspaper branch office was bombed, apparently to divert police, shortly before a U.S. Bank branch was bombed and robbed. About three months later a Planned Parenthood office was bombed shortly before the same bank branch was robbed.
There were no injuries in any of the bombings.
Federal authorities arrested three men near Yakima, Washington, after pursuing them from Portland, Oregon, where they allegedly were foiled in an effort to rob another U.S. Bank branch.
But authorities, citing witness accounts of the Spokane attacks, have long said they suspected a fourth person was involved.
The prosecution is expected to rest its case Monday against the first three suspects, who went on trial last week on explosives and bank robbery charges.
